data.name: Reflection of a Fallen Feather
data.detailed_description:
Trapped in a mysterious labyrinth – explore crystalline caverns, dim dungeons, and subterranean forested lakes in a quest to uncover an exit to the surface. Jump, smash, swim, and manipulate the environment to unveil artifacts used to access new areas or to strengthen your party in turn-based battles against the dangerous hordes wandering the labyrinth. To survive, transform into defeated enemies, and mix and match enemy abilities to create custom classes for your characters.

Features:

  • become the enemy—50 playable character types
  • full character customization—150 unique character abilities
  • hidden loot—dozens of unique accessories and tools
  • interactive open-world environment
  • fast-paced battle system—identify and exploit enemy weaknesses

data.short_description: In Reflection of a Fallen Feather you are the enemy. Triumph in turn-based battles to transform into defeated monsters - each party member is a fusion of three monster types with near infinite customization. Find hidden treasures used to jump, smash, swim, and manipulate the environment.

reviews.review:
This game is a weird piece of something. If the premise wasn't great on its own, the game itself is rather... crunchy.

I totally didn't expect these kinds of strategizing in battles trying to cover one party member's weakness with the other, the active switching and the overall trying to find the logic and memorize each foe's weakness/resistances through such simple and effective mechanics.
While I haven't played much, I've been to three very interestingly designed areas that got me hooked right away. I absolutely loved how it keeps itself extremely simple, clear and relies totally on great game and level design to keep things together.

Pros:
>Progress system based on transforming into defeated opponents, with the ability to keep some of their skills to create a nice and balanced party. This is done in a very clear way and everything you need to know is displayed in a direct manner.
>Battles are interesting, foes can be easily beat through knowledge and good transformation planning. 
>Combat system fully explained through itself. No wondering if this stat does that as EVERY skill has on its description what stat it uses and its element/cooldown/power/effect. 
>You can play as a spider.
>Map design is well made, with several shortcuts and small puzzles to keep travelling interesting.
>Music is a plus. 
>Writing is intricate. Dialogues kept me wondering every time someone had something to say. I look forward to find new NPCs to talk to even though I don't really understand much yet.

Cons:
>It's not the prettiest thing out there, even with its own aesthetics taken into account, it does get somewhat hard to discern what is there and what isn't. I like how a detailed lamia lady turns into a small snake when you get her as a party member, though.
>It can get very confusing though it's very simple.
>Lack an Options menu. Can't even change the sound/music volume or pick a resolution. 
>Whatever there is for a story isn't clear at all, though amusing due to its style.

Neutral:
>The game requires a lot of attention and memory. It doesn't hold your hand and expects a lot of the player, especially on the travelling side, as map design is far from straightforward. It's very easy to get completely lost.
>I miss health bars.

Overall, it makes up for a fun but demanding time and its a steal to be completely free. Just go and play it regardless.
